class.name: InputAction
class.brief_description: One action of the [InputMap] as a resource: its name, deadzone and events.
class.description: An [InputAction] describes one action of the [InputMap] ([code]"jump"[/code], [code]"ui_accept"[/code], ...) with its [member action] name, its [member deadzone] and its [member events]. The layers of the [InputMap] are [InputActions] of [InputAction]s: [method InputMap.get_input_action] returns the action of the [InputMap] itself (changing it changes the [InputMap]), and [method InputMap.set_input_action] puts one into the [InputMap]. A set of actions is an [InputActions]. [InputMapSettingsServer] stores the player's bindings as [InputActions]. [member events] is a list of [InputEvent]s. It is stored like any other resource property: a [code].tres[/code] file holds the events as sub-resources, the same layout the editor writes, so an [InputAction] or an [InputActions] can be edited in the Inspector and saved again. [InputMapSettingsServer] stores the player's bindings in readable text instead (see [method InputMapSettingsServer.events_to_text]). [method event_to_text] and [method text_to_event] convert one event to and from its text form The grammar is [code][Device<N>:]<Type>:[<Modifiers>+]<Input>[/code]. Only keys, mouse buttons, gamepad buttons and gamepad axes have one. Examples: [code]Keyboard:W[/code], [code]Keyboard:Ctrl+Shift+S[/code], [code]Keyboard:CmdOrCtrl+Z[/code], [code]Keyboard:Colon[/code], [code]Keyboard:Shift+Semicolon[/code], [code]Keyboard:Ctrl+Plus[/code], [code]Keyboard:Shift[/code], [code]KeyboardLabel:W[/code], [code]Mouse:Ctrl+Left[/code], [code]Gamepad:LeftShoulder[/code], [code]GamepadAxis:LeftStickLeft[/code], [code]Device3:Gamepad:A[/code], [code]Device3:GamepadAxis:RightTrigger[/code]. - [code]Device<N>:[/code] (optional): only the gamepad with this device number ([member InputEvent.device]). Without it the event reacts to all devices; [code]Any:[/code] is read as well, and so is the [code]@N[/code] suffix of older texts. It is written only for gamepad events of one pad; keys and mouse buttons are always bound for all devices (the prefix is read, not kept). - Type: [code]Keyboard[/code] (an [InputEventKey] matched by [member InputEventKey.physical_keycode], the key at the same place on every layout, the usual choice for games), [code]KeyboardLabel[/code] ([member InputEventKey.keycode]), [code]KeyboardPrinted[/code] ([member InputEventKey.key_label]), [code]Mouse[/code] ([InputEventMouseButton]), [code]Gamepad[/code] ([InputEventJoypadButton]) and [code]GamepadAxis[/code] ([InputEventJoypadMotion]). The older names [code]PhysicalKey[/code], [code]Key[/code], [code]KeyLabel[/code], [code]MouseButton[/code], [code]JoypadButton[/code] and [code]JoypadMotion[/code] are still read. - Modifiers (only [code]Keyboard*[/code] and [code]Mouse[/code]): [code]CmdOrCtrl[/code] ([member InputEventWithModifiers.command_or_control_autoremap]: Command on macOS, Ctrl on the other platforms), [code]Ctrl[/code], [code]Alt[/code], [code]Shift[/code] and [code]Meta[/code]. They are written in this order and read in any order. A modifier key alone is the input itself ([code]Keyboard:Shift[/code]). - Input of a key: a name of [method OS.get_keycode_string], never a character ([code]Colon[/code], [code]Semicolon[/code], [code]Plus[/code], [code]Minus[/code], [code]At[/code], [code]Space[/code]), so [code]:[/code] and [code]+[/code] stay separators; unknown codes are written as [code]#[/code] and the number. - Input of a mouse button: [code]Left[/code], [code]Right[/code], [code]Middle[/code], [code]WheelUp[/code], [code]WheelDown[/code], [code]WheelLeft[/code], [code]WheelRight[/code], [code]Extra1[/code] or [code]Extra2[/code]. - Input of a gamepad button: [code]A[/code], [code]B[/code], [code]X[/code], [code]Y[/code] (positions, [code]A[/code] is the bottom one), [code]LeftShoulder[/code], [code]RightShoulder[/code], [code]DPadUp[/code], [code]DPadDown[/code], [code]DPadLeft[/code], [code]DPadRight[/code], [code]Back[/code], [code]Start[/code], [code]Guide[/code], [code]LeftStickPress[/code], [code]RightStickPress[/code], [code]Misc1[/code], [code]Paddle1[/code] to [code]Paddle4[/code], [code]Touchpad[/code], or the button index. [code]LeftStick[/code] and [code]RightStick[/code] are read as the stick clicks. - Input of a gamepad axis, with the direction in the name: [code]LeftStickLeft[/code], [code]LeftStickRight[/code], [code]LeftStickUp[/code], [code]LeftStickDown[/code], the same for [code]RightStick[/code], [code]LeftTrigger[/code] and [code]RightTrigger[/code]. Other axes are written as the index with [code]+[/code] or [code]-[/code]. The older names with a sign ([code]LeftX-[/code], [code]LeftY+[/code], [code]TriggerRight+[/code]) are still read; [code]GamepadAxis:LeftStickX-[/code] is not valid. Not valid are, for example, [code]Gamepad:Ctrl+A[/code] (a gamepad has no modifiers), [code]Device:Gamepad:A[/code], [code]DeviceX:Gamepad:A[/code], [code]Keyboard:[/code], [code]Keyboard:Ctrl+[/code], an unknown type and an unknown key. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var action = InputAction.new() action.action = &"jump" action.deadzone = 0.3 action.add_event(InputAction.text_to_event("Keyboard:Space")) action.add_event(InputAction.text_to_event("Gamepad:A")) InputMap.set_input_action(action) ResourceSaver.save(action, "user://jump.tres") # The events are sub-resources of the file. [/gdscript] [csharp] var action = new InputAction(); action.Action = "jump"; action.Deadzone = 0.3f; action.AddEvent(InputAction.TextToEvent("Keyboard:Space")); action.AddEvent(InputAction.TextToEvent("Gamepad:A")); InputMap.Singleton.SetInputAction(action); ResourceSaver.Save(action, "user://jump.tres"); // The events are sub-resources of the file. [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

method.name: add_event
method.description: Adds [param event] to [member events]. Does nothing if the action already has the event (see [method has_event]).

method.name: clear_events
method.description: Removes all events from the action.

method.name: event_to_text
method.description: Returns the text form [code][Device<N>:]<Type>:[<Modifiers>+]<Input>[/code] of [param event] (see the class description), or an empty [String] for event types that have none (touch, MIDI, ...). Examples: [code]Keyboard:W[/code], [code]Keyboard:Ctrl+Shift+S[/code], [code]Keyboard:CmdOrCtrl+Z[/code], [code]Keyboard:Colon[/code], [code]Keyboard:Shift+Semicolon[/code], [code]Keyboard:Ctrl+Plus[/code], [code]Keyboard:Shift[/code], [code]KeyboardLabel:W[/code], [code]Mouse:Ctrl+Left[/code], [code]Gamepad:LeftShoulder[/code], [code]GamepadAxis:LeftStickLeft[/code], [code]Device3:Gamepad:A[/code], [code]Device3:GamepadAxis:RightTrigger[/code]. A key the player presses has all three codes; it is written as [code]Keyboard[/code], so the binding stays on the same key position on every keyboard layout. A modifier key on its own ([code]Keyboard:Shift[/code]) is written without modifiers. A gamepad event of one pad ([member InputEvent.device] [code]0[/code] or more) starts with [code]Device<N>:[/code].

method.name: get_device_events
method.description: Returns the events of [param device] in the order of [member events]. For example [constant INPUT_DEVICE_KEYBOARD] returns all keys of the action.

method.name: get_event_count
method.description: Returns the number of events of the action.

method.name: get_event_device
method.description: Returns the device that [param event] belongs to: [constant INPUT_DEVICE_KEYBOARD] for an [InputEventKey], [constant INPUT_DEVICE_MOUSE] for an [InputEventMouseButton], [constant INPUT_DEVICE_GAMEPAD] for an [InputEventJoypadButton] or [InputEventJoypadMotion], and [constant INPUT_DEVICE_MAX] for event types that can't be bound.

method.name: has_event
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the action has [param event] itself or an event that matches it exactly (see [method InputEvent.is_match] with [code]exact_match[/code] set to [code]true[/code]).

method.name: remove_event
method.description: Removes [param event] or the first event that matches it exactly (see [method has_event]) from the action. Returns [code]true[/code] if an event was removed, [code]false[/code] if the action has no such event.

method.name: text_to_event
method.description: Returns a new event of the text form [param text] ([code][Device<N>:]<Type>:[<Modifiers>+]<Input>[/code], see the class description), or [code]null[/code] if the text is not valid. Examples: [code]Keyboard:W[/code], [code]Keyboard:Ctrl+Shift+S[/code], [code]Keyboard:CmdOrCtrl+Z[/code], [code]Keyboard:Colon[/code], [code]Keyboard:Shift+Semicolon[/code], [code]Keyboard:Ctrl+Plus[/code], [code]Keyboard:Shift[/code], [code]KeyboardLabel:W[/code], [code]Mouse:Ctrl+Left[/code], [code]Gamepad:LeftShoulder[/code], [code]GamepadAxis:LeftStickLeft[/code], [code]Device3:Gamepad:A[/code], [code]Device3:GamepadAxis:RightTrigger[/code]. Its [member InputEvent.device] is the number of the [code]Device<N>:[/code] prefix for a gamepad event, otherwise [code]-1[/code] (all devices). [code]CmdOrCtrl[/code] is resolved here: the event uses [member InputEventWithModifiers.command_or_control_autoremap].

members.member: The name of the action in the [InputMap], for example [code]&"jump"[/code]. The property is not called [code]name[/code], because [member Resource.resource_name] already uses that name.
The deadzone of the action, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code] (see [method InputMap.action_set_deadzone]).

The events that trigger the action, shown in the Inspector and stored as sub-resources. Setting it replaces all events; [code]null[/code] entries are skipped. The getter returns a new array: change the events with [method add_event], [method remove_event] and [method clear_events], or set the whole list.

constants.constant: A mouse button or the mouse wheel ([InputEventMouseButton]).
The number of devices; also returned by [method get_event_device] for events that can't be bound.
